# Release 0 contract fixture corpus

`bin/*.bin` contains committed raw binary fixture bundles. Each bundle uses a test-only 44-byte `R0FXBIN\0` envelope followed by the exact raw handoff, memory-map, and RHD byte sequences. The envelope carries only fixture lengths, expected result, and an injected trusted window for the host oracle; it is not a RAR OS public contract and does not decide the pre-copy trust boundary proposed in ADR 0013.

`generate.sh` deterministically recreates every binary from `cases.v1`. `run.sh` compares regenerated bytes with the committed corpus. In the pinned Linux CI route, `reference.rs` is compiled as host-only code and parses the raw bytes with checked unsigned arithmetic. It computes normalized x86-64/AArch64 semantic equality rather than trusting a fixture-authored label.

The corpus covers the R0-002 packet's required truncated, oversized, misaligned, overlapping, unknown-critical, invalid-pointer, and architecture-inconsistent classes plus valid and maximum-size boundaries. Each current negative fixture has one intended fault so it does not choose unresolved multi-fault precedence. MMIO authority, record-identity policy, and compound-fault precedence cases remain blocked on proposed ADRs 0013–0015 and must be added when those decisions are approved.
